title: Starship goes orbital.
summary: Orbit achieved. 26 Starlink V3 satellites deployed. A new chapter in the Starship story.
details: Starship reached Earth orbit for the first time after an in-space insertion burn, then deployed 26 operational Starlink V3 satellites.
An engine shut down during ascent. The remaining engines compensated, and flight controllers approved orbital operations after checking the systems needed to return.
The team chose an early deorbit as a precaution. Starship reentered and splashed down in the northern Pacific; Super Heavy completed its planned ocean landing sequence.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 14 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: A landing worth the wait.
summary: Twenty V3 satellites deployed on a suborbital path. Starship returned intact to the Indian Ocean.
details: The second V3 mission deployed 20 Starlink V3 satellites on a deliberately suborbital trajectory. Communications with every satellite were demonstrated before reentry.
Starship relit a Raptor in space, survived reentry and performed a controlled landing. It remained intact and floating after splashdown.
Super Heavy completed the high-thrust part of boostback but ended the burn early. Only a subset of engines restarted for landing, resulting in a hard splashdown.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 13 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: Meet the next generation.
summary: V3, Raptor 3, and a new launch pad. The next generation made its debut above Starbase.
details: Flight 12 introduced the V3 vehicles, Raptor 3 engines and Pad 2. Starship reached its planned trajectory despite losing a vacuum engine during ascent.
The ship deployed 20 simulators and two modified Starlink satellites for in-space imaging, then reentered and splashed down using two engines.
The booster could not ignite all intended boostback engines and made a hard ocean splashdown.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 12 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: One last flight. All objectives.
summary: The V2 era closed with payload deployment, an engine relight, and two controlled splashdowns.
details: The last second-generation Starship flight achieved every major objective. Eight Starlink simulators were deployed and a Raptor relit in space.
Starship tested its heat shield and a banking maneuver before a controlled landing in the Indian Ocean.
The booster used a landing-burn profile intended for the next generation and splashed down as planned.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 11 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: Back on course.
summary: The first successful payload deployment. Eight simulators released, with both vehicles returning to the ocean.
details: Starship successfully deployed eight Starlink simulators, its first payload deployment demonstration, and relit a Raptor in space.
The ship survived a deliberately demanding reentry and performed a controlled Indian Ocean splashdown.
Super Heavy tested a backup landing engine and completed a soft splashdown. All major objectives were achieved.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 10 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: Fly. Learn. Fly again.
summary: A Super Heavy flew for the second time. The ship reached space but lost control during coast.
details: For the first time, a previously flown Super Heavy launched again. It completed ascent, then tested a higher angle of attack during descent before breaking apart during landing burn.
Starship completed its ascent, but its payload door failed to open. An attitude-control problem prevented the engine relight and a controlled reentry.
Contact with Starship ended roughly 46 minutes into flight.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 9 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: Another catch. More to learn.
summary: Super Heavy returned to the tower. The upper stage was lost after engine failures during ascent.
details: The booster completed its return to Starbase and became the third Super Heavy caught by the tower.
An energetic event in Starship’s aft section caused several engines to fail. The ship lost attitude control and communications about nine and a half minutes after launch.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 8 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: A new ship takes the stage.
summary: The first V2 Starship launched. The booster was caught, while the ship was lost during ascent.
details: The first flight of the upgraded Starship upper stage tested a substantially redesigned vehicle.
Super Heavy returned to the launch tower for the program’s second successful catch.
A fire developed in the aft section of Starship. Contact ended about eight and a half minutes into flight, before ascent was complete.

title: Restarting in space.
summary: A Raptor relit in space for the first time. Both stages made controlled ocean splashdowns.
details: Starship relit a single Raptor in space, proving a capability needed to leave orbit safely on future missions.
Automatic launch-tower checks ruled out a booster catch. Super Heavy diverted to its planned ocean landing area.
The ship tested heat-shield changes and a steeper descent, then completed a daylight splashdown in the Indian Ocean.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 6 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: Caught. On the first try.
summary: The tower caught Super Heavy in midair. A defining moment for reusable spaceflight.
details: Super Heavy returned to Starbase and was caught by the launch tower’s arms on the very first attempt. Thousands of vehicle and pad checks had to pass before the approach.
Starship completed its ascent, controlled reentry and landing burn, splashing down in the Indian Ocean about 66 minutes after launch.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 5 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: All the way back down.
summary: For the first time, both vehicles survived the return and completed soft ocean splashdowns.
details: Super Heavy performed its first soft splashdown after a controlled boostback and landing burn.
Starship maintained control through atmospheric reentry and severe heating. Despite damage, it performed its flip and landing burn to reach the ocean.
The mission demonstrated the return techniques needed for eventual recovery and reuse.

title: A window into reentry.
summary: Starship completed ascent, tested its payload door and propellant transfer, then reached atmospheric entry.
details: Starship completed a full-duration ascent burn for the first time and coasted on a suborbital trajectory. It tested the payload door and initiated an internal propellant-transfer demonstration.
Excessive rolling prevented an in-space engine relight. The ship was lost during atmospheric entry, with the last data received around 49 minutes into flight.
Super Heavy attempted its landing burn but broke apart above the ocean.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 3 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: The first taste of space.
summary: All 33 booster engines completed ascent. Hot staging worked, and Starship crossed the edge of space.
details: All 33 Super Heavy engines completed their ascent burn. Starship ignited its own engines before separating in the first successful hot-staging maneuver.
The booster broke apart after beginning boostback. The ship reached approximately 150 kilometers altitude before its flight termination system was triggered near the end of ascent.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 2 campaign, photographed by Max Evans

title: Every journey has a first.
summary: The full Starship stack lifted off for the first time, clearing the tower and beginning a new era of testing.
details: The first integrated Starship and Super Heavy test cleared the launch tower and climbed for several minutes.
Multiple engines failed during ascent. The vehicle did not separate, lost control and was terminated over the Gulf.
The flight informed major changes to the launch pad, engine reliability and stage-separation system.

photo.alt: Starship Flight 1 campaign, photographed by Max Evans
